Listen to this article Share An Algerian army convoy has arrived in Niger in Algeria’s first foreign troop deployment since it sent ​forces to support Egypt during the 1973 Arab-Israeli ‌war. Niger, like other countries in West Africa’s Sahel region, is battling insurgents linked to al Qaeda and Islamic State Algeria, which ​shares a border with Niger, has traditionally regarded ​stability in the Sahel-Sahara as an important regional ⁠security priority. Energy is an important focus for Algeria in ​Niger, where Algerian state-run oil and gas firm Sonatrach has investments One ​major project, the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline with Niger and Nigeria, aims to deliver African gas to Europe and other international markets. Reuters ​spoke to 10 people who said the first Algerian ​military convoy had reached Arlit, a uranium mining town in the ‌country’s ⁠northwest. Algeria has said the decision to deploy troops was taken to protect the country’s energy and economic interests, without disclosing the size of the force or the timetable ​for their arrival. Military ​officers have ⁠ruled Niger, which has uranium, oil and gold resources, since the July 2023 coup ​that ousted President Mohamed Bazoum, which Algeria ​initially opposed. The ⁠deployment is a sign that relations between Algiers and Niamey have improved since last year, when Niger recalled its ⁠ambassador ​from Algeria, after Mali accused ​Algeria of shooting down one of its drones near the border.
